## Join the Rose Lab

I'm joining the JMU Geography department in spring 2027, and I'm looking for undergraduates who are curious about how landscapes change: why wildflowers bloom when they do, how oak woodlands recover after fire, or what South Africa's coast looked like hundreds of thousands of years ago.

**You don't need prior research experience.** Curiosity, reliability, and a willingness to learn new tools matter more than what you already know!

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### What students in the lab do

Depending on the project and your interests, you might:

- 🛰️ Work with satellite and airborne imagery to map vegetation change
- 🌼 Help connect field observations of flowering to what we can see from the sky (or space)
- 💻 Learn to analyze and map environmental data in R
- 📊 Build maps and figures that help land managers make conservation decisions
- 🗣️ Present your work at JMU events or at regional and national conferences

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Ways to get involved

- **Paid research assistantship.** Want to help build GIS and remote sensing tools for improving oak conservation? I will be recruiting several multi-year research assistants to help process remote sensing data, build ecologial models, and develop a user-friendly tool that will be used by The Nature Conservancy and other land managers in California.
- **Independent study or research credit.** Work on a piece of an ongoing project for course credit.
- **Honors or senior thesis.** Develop your own question related to vegetation change, remote sensing, or biogeography.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Courses I teach at JMU

- **Spring 2027:** GEOG 385: Digital Image Processing in Remote Sensing, a hands-on course on using remote sensing to map environmental change.
- **Fall 2027:** TBD!

Taking one of my courses is a great way to see whether the lab is a good fit.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### How to reach out

Send me an email at [mbrose@sdsu.edu](mailto:mbrose@sdsu.edu) (a JMU address is coming soon!) with:

1. Your year and major
2. A few sentences about what interests you (it's fine if it's broad!)
3. Any relevant courses or experience (none is fine too)

I read every email, and I'm happy to meet even if you just want to chat about your interests and what you can do with a Geography degree.
